children: Banking stocks rallied on Thursday morning after the Reserve Bank of India's overseas capital-raising measures brought in a much stronger-than-expected $136.38 billion in foreign currency inflows under FCNR(B). The Nifty Bank index rose 0.91 percent to 57,694.95 around 9:40 am, with ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, HDFC Bank and SBI among the top Nifty 50 gainers.

The rally was broad-based across the banking space. The Nifty Private Bank index gained 1.17 percent, while the Nifty PSU Bank index advanced 1.14 percent, placing all three banking indices among the top sectoral gainers.

Large private-sector lenders led the gains on the benchmark index. ICICI Bank climbed 1.59 percent to Rs 1,449.20, Axis Bank gained 1.55 percent to Rs 1,273.30 and HDFC Bank rose 1.28 percent to Rs 709.80. SBI was up 0.92 percent at Rs 1,030.30. The four lenders featured among the top 10 gainers on the Nifty 50.

The strength extended to midcap banking stocks. Bank of Maharashtra jumped nearly 4 percent to Rs 85.25, while Punjab & Sind Bank gained 3 percent to Rs 23.31. Bandhan Bank advanced 2.32 percent to Rs 165.45 and Bank of India rose 2.04 percent to Rs 145.40. Four banks were among the top gainers on the BSE Midcap index.
Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today

Banking stocks outperformed while the broader market staged a relief rally. At 9:40 am, the Sensex was up 303 points, or 0.40 percent, at 76,873.51, while the Nifty 50 gained 96 points, or 0.40 percent, to 24,010.90. Market breadth was firmly positive, with 2,232 shares advancing against 914 declines.

The massive mobilisation through the RBI's special USD-INR forex swap facility has boosted liquidity in the banking system and strengthened India's external buffers. FCNR(B) deposits accounted for $127.23 billion of the total inflows as of August 31, while overseas foreign currency borrowings contributed $5.26 billion and external commercial borrowings another $3.89 billion. The overall mobilisation substantially exceeded earlier expectations.

The FCNR(B) deposit window closed on August 31, while the facility for ECBs and OFCBs will remain open until December 31. The RBI had introduced the special swap facility in June to attract foreign currency inflows at a time when capital outflows, a weakening rupee and elevated crude oil prices were putting pressure on India's external position.

The unexpectedly large foreign currency inflows also boosted the rupee. The domestic currency strengthened as much as 0.7 percent to around 94.27 against the dollar on Thursday, reaching its strongest level in more than a month.

Global cues provided further support after US President Donald Trump played down the prospect of a prolonged conflict with Iran. Asian equities rallied, while Brent crude paused its three-day surge and traded around $95.50 a barrel, easing some of the pressure that elevated oil prices had exerted on Indian assets.

The improvement in risk sentiment was also reflected in volatility, with the India VIX falling about 5 percent to 11.02. Among other sectors, the Nifty Realty index gained 1.51 percent and Nifty Metal rose 0.89 percent, while Nifty IT fell 1 percent and Nifty FMCG declined 0.46 percent.
